# Embers of the Hollow Sun: the rulebook

The one list of rules in force for the whole project (issue 492, FINDINGS R190). Each rule says what to do, why (the problem
Ryan was reacting to, in his words where they exist), who set it and when, and its old ids. Rules of play and balance numbers
are not here (R190's scope): they live in the browser oracle, godot/rules and their FINDINGS rows (for example battles growing
over a run toward about 20 ships, a guide and not a cap, R1; capture as add, strip or ransom, R4).

Ryan, Nov 11 2026: "Those old hard coded rules with no context or detail artifically restricing us are exactly what I'm worried
about across the board" (R190), and at 20:05 CST: "Let's ensure we're documenting all these decisions and approaches. I don't
want this drift to keep happening or where we get confused on how we're doing things."

Set by: **Ryan** (his own call, his words exist), **Board** (a Claude Board thread wrote it), **agent** (Muse, Codex or a
worker). Ids are FINDINGS rows (R, D, F, G, X) or register ids from contrib/opus/reviews/rules_sweep/.

## 0. How rules work here

0.1 **Every rule carries its reason, beside it.** Why: three old rules with no reason were built to the letter on Nov 11 (sliced
wrecks R186, the flash counter R187, the movement call R189). Ryan: "I think some of the findings got misinterpreted." Set:
Ryan, Nov 11 (R189, R190). A rule nobody can give a reason for does not go in this book.

0.2 **A ruling is landed only when the same pull request edits this book or the working document for its area** (the
playbook, RECIPE.md, AGENTS.md). Why: rulings filed in FINDINGS never reached the documents builders read (R209, R211). Set:
Ryan, Nov 11 (R214). FINDINGS stays as the dated history; this book is the live source. Each FINDINGS row from R281 on
says where it landed ("landed in <repo path>") or says "one-off job decision"; the memory lint
(contrib/opus/tools/memory_lint_tests.js) fails a row that says neither, so a ruling cannot sit in FINDINGS alone (R291,
issue 890).

0.3 **Which document wins.** This book; then the playbook for the area; then AGENTS.md; then briefs. HANDOFF.md and LOOP.md
win for current status only. Between two of Ryan's rulings the later one wins, and the entry here is edited, never only a new
FINDINGS row. Why: corrections written as new rows left the old wording reading as the rule (R183's withdrawn gate line).
Set: Board, Nov 11, from Muse's outside sweep (contrib/muse/reviews/rules_sweep_2026_11.md, Parts 4 and 6).

0.4 **A number in a document is a starting point judged by eye, unless it protects comfort, frame rate, saves, crashes or rules
parity.** A number names its measurement, or says it is a tuning value. Why: every hit size was tuned under a cap that was
never the guideline it cited (R187); Ryan wanted the audit to find "these weird arbitrary, like, guidance on that is making
it, you know, more restricted and less realistic and cinematic than it should be". Set: Ryan, Nov 7 (R121: assumed gates stop
binding until a measurement earns them back) and Nov 11 (R187: "Keep comfort, loosen rest").

0.5 **Order follows the faction; motion and breaks never feel staged.** Hullbreaker armour is irregular patchwork. Eclipse
panels are precise, dead even, ordered and aligned, with seams and slight relief (Ryan, Nov 13, R243: "make the eclipse panels
actually panels and dead even and ordered to align"). Glasswrights are blown glass without panels; Chorus surfaces are grown,
without plates. Sunward and Hegemony follow factions.md. Instant motion, identical beats, straight cuts and one scale still
read as staged. Why: the wrecks "feel like they're just getting sliced in half" (R186); applying that to every faction's
surface erased the Eclipse's machine precision. Set: Ryan's complaints, Board's wording (R187), corrected by Ryan (R243).

0.6 **A rule that rests on a fact that can change names what ends it** (a model's version, a plan's limit, a tool that is
down). Why: the Codex cloud ban, the Fable helper counts and the Kimi sentence outlived their facts. Set: Board, Nov 11 (Muse
sweep Part 4).

0.7 **A rule that says the game does something needs a capture or a check that shows it, or the words "not built yet".** Why:
specs described braking jets and slow motion the game did not have (issue 492). Set: Board, Nov 11.

0.8 **After a day with many rulings, the Board has an outside model check that each one landed in the document a worker reads
(a dropped-context sweep).** Batch rulings that only set a rule (no working method) may land in this book alone. Why: the
insides rule was recorded but never reached the builder's playbook (R209, R211); Muse's method audit found
the screens half of R218 written nowhere (issue 558). Set: Board, Nov 12 (R211, issue 558).

0.9 **How a route is set up (any multi-step pipeline: ships, effects, captures, installs).** (a) A method change is done
only when one real item has gone end to end through it into the game on Ryan's PC; each stage passing alone is not a pass.
(b) Each fact has one home: the first step that decides it writes it, and every later step reads it from there instead of
keeping its own copy; a mirror refreshed from that home under a check (the oracle copies, 12.4) is not a second home. (c) A check tests what its rule says and reads the item's own numbers (length, seams, part shapes),
never the shape of the first item it was written for. (d) Anything Ryan's PC runs (.bat launchers, installs, caches) gets
one real run there before it counts as done, within 3.3 (nothing deleted on the PC without Ryan's yes). No new test or gate is added for this rule; it shapes how routes are built
and briefed. Why: Codex's A16 dry run (issue 587) found eight gaps from these four habits: the build sheet and the recipe
kept separate copies of the same facts, three checks assumed the old C15s cruiser (its 14.5 length, an extra seam,
closed engine bells), a launcher quoting bug and a stale game cache only show on Windows in a real install, and no ship
had gone from sheet to game since the sheet method changed. Set: Board, Nov 12, on Ryan's ask to learn from the gaps at
the level of design and setup, not patches (R225).


0.10 **How the repo carries memory (R251).** A standing rule comes only from Ryan's words, quoted in FINDINGS and landed here; a row
that stretches his words past what he named says so and asks him. Board choices for one day or one job (effort, caps, job order,
wrappers, which seat took a job) are operating notes in LOOP.md, never rules. A new ruling names what it replaces and the old row is
marked SUPERSEDED, so no two live rules conflict. One live place per kind: rules in this book, what is open and who has it on GitHub itself
(checked live before any dispatch; contrib/opus/OPEN_WORK.md is only a timestamped nightly index of it, issue 890), what runs on the PC in LOOP.md's newest LATEST lines and The seats, the hand-over in HANDOFF section 0 (about one page; older sections go to docs/archive), history in FINDINGS.
LOOP.md's LATEST lines roll into a dated summary once they pass about 15. Muse audits for stale or conflicting docs now and then.
Why: several models and fresh chats read the repo cold; on Nov 14 a one-day choice nearly became a rule, an A20 note was stretched to
every ship before Ryan ratified it (R244), and a summary line inverted Ryan's call on A18 and A19.

## 1. Working with Ryan

1.1 **Plain words, the answer first, your pick and why; no em dashes; no human-hour estimates** (estimate in agent runs and
review rounds from the board's own history). Why: he is not a coder; and "every time estimate has been wildly off. its human
based, not multiple LLMs and agent based." Set: Ryan (AGENTS.md; R99, Nov 4). Ids: agents-31, agents-36, R99d.

1.2 **Pictures for anything visual: one per item, its code name on it, about 1280 px wide and no taller than 720 px.** Why: he
judges by pictures, cannot see tall stacked sheets, and "I can't tell which one is a11" (R185). Set: Ryan (R185, Nov 11);
sizes Board (HANDOFF). Ids: agents-32, handoff-05, R185c.

1.3 **When Ryan points at a picture from memory, find it and show it with its code name before building on it.** Why: the
Board read "our prior concept" as the wrong picture and three rounds were drawn against it (R196). Set: Board, Nov 11.

1.4 **Anything he runs himself is a double-click .bat** (Windows 10, PowerShell 5.1, no Python of his own). Why: not a coder.
Set: Ryan. Id: agents-33.

1.5 **Before anything bigger than a quick fix, ask 3 to 5 plain multiple-choice scope questions in one batch**, each choice
said as what he will see. Why: he steers by picks ("Options first, then build", R167). Set: Ryan. Ids: agents-34,
musebrief-03.

1.6 **Questions for Ryan go to him in the agent's own chat, never as GitHub tags or comments; message him only when something
lands or needs him: two lines and one image.** Why: his own instruction on where he reads (Nov 2) and what he wants to see.
Set: Ryan. Ids: agents-11, loop-05.

1.7 **Picks, looks and money are Ryan's.** Payments, top-ups and sign-ups stay his. Why: his game and his accounts. Set: Ryan
(AGENTS.md seat table; R126b).

## 2. The Board and the agents

2.1 **The Board owns the whole board.** One Claude thread in the Project (Opus 5.5 since Nov 11) holds design calls, the final
technical call and every merge; it starts agreed work on its own, picks the seat, keeps contrib/opus/OPEN_WORK.md moving, and
asks Ryan only for design, key decisions, reviews of what he will see, and conflicts. Why: agreed items were left behind
whenever new work arrived ("The station is a good example of something we already aligned on but is still sitting there",
R194); and "you own the codebase and github. you are my orchestrator and control the building" (R202). Set: Ryan, Nov 8 to 11
(R119: "sure merge, you're the owner now"; R167, R194, R202). Duties: contrib/opus/LOOP.md "The Board's standing duties".

2.2 **Nobody grades their own work.** Workers never merge their own pull requests. An Opus-built, game-facing change gets an
outside check (Muse, issue 256) before or straight after merge; a tools-only pull request that other jobs wait on may merge on
the Board's diff review while Muse is idle, with the check still asked for. Set: Ryan (R119, R132, R133, R167); the exception
Board (R162). Ids: agents-13, claude-04, R132c, R162b.

2.3 **Review every pull request by its diff, never its title, then sweep its impact** (every caller, saves and old profiles,
both rule twins, every UI path, which tests really ran), then the pictures. Merge only on green, and only after every check
job has finished. Why: a merged change left existing profiles with Heat closed (R129); PR 542 merged before its parity jobs
ended (LOOP, Nov 12). Set: Board (R129); Ryan's project instructions. Ids: R129a, loop-03.

Pictures carry their revision and stage. Every picture shown to Ryan is labelled with the revision that produced it and its
stage (sheet built, paint proof, installed in game, Ryan accepted); a stale picture is never shown as current, and if the
picture is stale the review stops there rather than judging it. A visual pull request merges only after its picture has been
compared with the concept and the ruling it answers, in a view that actually shows the feature being judged, and the Board
says plainly in the pull request where it misses. What a ruling can measure is measured on the painted output and reported
(the plate-character measure, issue 875); passing the countable checks is not visual acceptance. Why: the painted ships
passed fit, weapon match, triangles and density while missing their rulings, and a pre-fix picture was shown as the fix
(R289). Set: Board, Nov 16 2026 (issue 880).

2.4 **The job board is GitHub issues with owner labels, each opening with the fixed block** (Owner, Brief, Deliver to, Branch,
Effort or Models, Done when; optional `Base: <branch>`; ship builds add Route per part, Inside, Paint stack, Budget, R214). Agents deliver on
`codex/`, `muse/`, `work/` or `opus/issue-N` branches; nobody pushes to main except LOOP.md and FINDINGS. Why: any agent can
pick up a job without asking, and main stays reviewed. Set: Ryan, Nov 2 and 4 (R75, R102). Ids: agents-04, agents-05,
agents-09. A run brief for a PC job goes into the issue body (under the fixed block, marked as the job now): the runner
builds the task from the body only and never reads comments (R281).
When the Board needs Ryan's answer on a job, it adds the `ryan` label and one issue-body line `Ask Ryan: <one question> | Picture: <link>`, then removes both when he answers; Mission Control reads only this marker so it cannot mistake a dispatch lock for a question (Ryan, Nov 17, issue 951).
The PC runner merges `origin/<branch>` from the optional Base line and commits that merge before starting the agent;
a conflict stops before the agent with the checkout kept. Briefs name Base instead of asking an agent to merge while
also forbidding commits. The runner sets the running label and one status comment per job branch (edited in place on
retries and at the end), naming seat, machine, lane folder, branch, start time, ceiling, last commit and how to resume.
Before checkout or model calls, every PC runner refuses closed or running jobs and a delivery branch or open PR for the job from another seat prefix (same-prefix reruns are allowed); a body with exactly one fixed block and no run history needs no marker and is passed whole, otherwise exactly one line outside code fences containing `THIS IS THE JOB NOW` in heading, bold or plain form selects the fixed block plus that run; Effort (Codex) is required only for Codex, and the label and status comment must be set and read back before work, while later reporting failures are logged without changing the result (R291, issue 888). It clears its own running claim at the end. Why: merge-left partials
on 800, 815 and 44, and jobs with no visible running seat. Set: Ryan R270, issue 846 (788 step 3).

One current instruction. A job's current run brief sits at the top of its issue body, under the fixed block, marked as the
job now; older runs are marked done in the body. A brief in a comment is not an instruction: the PC runner builds the task
from the body only, so a comment brief silently reruns the old job. Why: 373 run 3 was briefed in a comment and came back
as a rerun of run 2. Set: Board (R281).

An open issue is not proof the work is undone. Issues here stay open after their pull requests merge (2.5), so before
queueing or relabelling an issue, search for a merged pull request that names it; on every merge, close the issue in the
same step when its scope is done, and where a merge is partial, say what scope remains. Artoo's dispatch sweep (2.7)
lists open issues with merged pull requests before each queueing round; the sweep is the audit, not the mechanism. Why:
780, 781, 783 and 824 were queued again after pull requests 796, 787, 825 and 832 had merged (Ryan: "Why did you miss all
those old jobs were already merged? That's a big miss."). Set: Board (R288).

2.5 **Never write a GitHub closing word before an issue number in a commit; use `gh api` REST, never GraphQL.** Why: commit
1429ca3 closed PR 320 by accident; GraphQL is blocked here (ends when it is unblocked). Set: Board. Ids: loop-15, loop-20.

# The Fable program: one finished battle, and playbooks other models can run

Issue 405. FINDINGS R167. Written by the Board (Fable 5.2), Nov 10 2026.

## What Ryan asked for

"I still have another full fable reset, so we can use fable on the really key stuff. Design, graphics, effects, etc. let's do
everything we can to use the fable resets smart here. Playbooks or recipes, deep reviews and redesign, etc. codebase is yours
with my direction and vision, you bring it to life with the decisions needed from me. I want this to end with something that
opus or other models can run from" (Nov 10 2026, 08:42 CST).

His scope answers:
- Focus, in this order of weight: battle effects, ships, space and the board. Screens and sound still get a playbook, lighter.
- End state: "One finished battle + playbooks".
- Steering: "Options first, then build". He sees two or three options, picks one, then it is built.
- Decisions: "As they come". Two lines and one image, whenever a pick is ready.

## The end state

1. **One finished battle.** A single fight that looks and reads final from the first shot to the last wreck, at the camera the
   game is really played at (camera 170 on the look bench). It is the proof that the recipes work and the reference every
   later job is judged against.
2. **A playbook per area**, written from what that battle needed, so another model can do the next ship, effect, hex or
   screen without asking: docs/playbooks/effects.md, ships.md, space.md, screens.md, sound.md.
3. **The front door**: HANDOFF.md section 0 and AGENTS.md point at the playbooks, and the job board holds the remaining items
   as ready jobs written from each playbook's job template.

## The finished battle (what "final" means here)

- **Board**: the dead-star gravity-well board (owner ruling, Oct 24).
- **Fleets**: about six to eight ships a side. **Sunward Crusade against Eclipse** (Ryan, Nov 11 2026, R180; this replaces the
  first plan of the Hullbreakers plus one other). Both have a settled flagship (docs/playbooks/factions.md) and look nothing
  alike. Each fleet needs one capital, one cruiser or destroyer and one escort through the ship recipe.
- **Ships**: built by tools/recipe with real thickness and comprehensive insides (R98, R209, R215), hard points by hull class
  and faction theme (R164 item 4, issue 363), from an accepted concept in the one style (R197) and an Opus build sheet that
  passes the concept standard (R203, R205, R207; docs/playbooks/ships.md).
- **Effects**: every big moment staged to Muse's table (contrib/muse/design/hit_staging_2026_11/synthesis.md): explosions by
  the picked route (issues 353, 365), deaths in three beats (366), one kit of trails, beams and flares (367), effects that
  start on the ship (370), shields that hug the hull with one shield pool, per-side coverage and lossy power routing, resting as Rim and Gap (R246 replaces R163 item 2's four strengths and invisible rest; 371 rules first, then 372 the look; design in contrib/muse/design/shields_2026_11/).
- **Space**: nebula and ion storm hexes with depth (368), a board planet and rocks from real data, remixed past recognition
  (R163 item 3; 369), the black hole and sky calm enough that ships and effects win.
- **Screen**: the battle screen in the ember orders-sheet look, layout E1 Ledger, shield readouts in Glacier #92b8e8 (Ryan,
  Nov 11: "Retire lime", R191; "E1 Ledger" and "Glacier pale blue", R210). Being built: issue 271 step 2.
- **Sound**: scoped (R171: weapons, hits and deaths, buttons and menus, ambience, music; "Clean and tactical"). Routing is in
  (issue 506); sound weight is next (R193 (4)); the redo follows the listening page.
- **Done**: a capture of the whole fight and its look bench sheet, and Ryan says yes.

## How every item flows

1. **Options.** Fable makes two or three options: a bench sheet of real captures where the thing exists, a flat mockup where
   it does not. Cheap, fast, and never more than one sheet per decision.
2. **Pick.** Ryan picks, with one image and two lines in front of him. The pick is recorded in FINDINGS with his words.
3. **Build.** The seat the table below names builds it. One worked example first, never the whole set.
4. **Proof.** The look bench before and after, at camera 170 first (bench a commit twice, keep the second run), plus the
   area's own check. Fable looks at the pictures, not the claim.
5. **Recipe.** What worked is written into the area's playbook the same day: target, steps, check, traps, job template.
6. **Roll out.** The rest of that kind (the other 34 hulls, the other weapons, the other hexes) becomes jobs written from the
   playbook's template, for DeepSeek, Codex or Opus. Fable only reviews their pictures.

Standing rules for every flow (Nov 16 2026, issue 880): the run brief lives in the issue body, one current instruction
(R281); an open issue is not proof of undone work, and a merge closes its issue in the same step when its scope is done
(R288); every picture carries its revision and stage; and visual work is compared with its concept and ruling, with the
misses stated plainly, before it merges (RULEBOOK 2.3 and 2.4).

## The playbook format (every playbook, same headings)

1. **Target**: the pictures to match and Ryan's own words about them.
2. **Inputs**: what must exist before you start.
3. **Steps**: numbered, with the exact job files and commands.
4. **The check that proves it**: bench rows, cameras, numbers, and what a pass looks like.
5. **Traps**: what went wrong before, each with its FINDINGS row.
6. **Worked example**: the pull requests that did it once.
7. **Job template**: the issue block to copy for the next item of this kind.
8. **Seat**: who runs it, and when to hand a picture back to the Board.

A playbook is done when a model that has never seen this repo ships the next item from it and the Board changes nothing.

## Budget and pacing (rewritten Nov 11 2026 evening)

- Ryan's Fable resets are all used (R180). The Board and Opus workers draw the Claude plan: two Opus workers at most while the
  Board thread is active (the five-hour limit was hit on Nov 11 with three; LOOP.md duties item 9).
- Codex gives about 100 minutes of work per five-hour window; one Codex job per lane; GPU work sized to the job (RULEBOOK 3.4, R293).
- If a limit is hit, nothing stops: DeepSeek, Muse and Codex keep running the rows that are theirs, and the Board's picks wait
  in LOOP.md.

## 12. Automatic checks

12.1 **Checks protect crashes, saves, rules parity, comfort and frame rate. A test that pins a look number is updated in the
same pull request that changes the picked look.** Why: tests fixed hit sizes, piece counts and cue counts that the audit fixes
had to move (contrib/codex/reviews/rules_sweep_checks.md). Set: Board, Nov 11 (0.4).

12.2 **A check's state comes from the real functions, never typed by hand; missing things fail loudly; one source per fact.**
Why: a fixture typed by hand let 137 checks pass while real play was broken (R155). Set: Board, after the outside audit
(R154, R155). Ids: R155a, handoff-08.

12.3 **Every push to an agent branch runs the checks once; every test script under godot/**/test/ has its line in
godot/tools/ci/godot_checks.txt.** Why: a missing test must fail loudly (PR 400). Set: Board. Ids: handoff-07, loop-10.

12.4 **A change to data.js or battle.js names every copy it must refresh, and rules parity passes.** Why: the oracle copies
drifted (R155). Set: Board. Id: R155b.

12.5 **The look bench: bench a commit twice and keep the second run; a change differs where it is meant to and nowhere else;
a new baseline is committed only when the Board accepts the change.** Why: the first run pays for shader warm-up (R162).
Set: Board. Ids: R162c, program-07, skill-sv-02, skill-sv-03.

12.6 **The player-path recording of Battles 1 to 3 is the acceptance check for visual and teaching changes.** Use
`tools/pc/jobs/player_path.bat` on the shared installed build with a fresh, isolated profile and player defaults. Judge the change
in those recordings. Use the look bench and bot captures for comparison and diagnosis. Earlier captures hid the
cut-ins, danger overlay, teaching cards, target card and battle voice that a new player encounters. The look bench also
draws meshes at full detail. Set: Ryan, Nov 19 (R328).

421:func _glb_to_scene(path: String, out: String, name: String) -> bool:
422:	var doc := GLTFDocument.new()
423:	var st := GLTFState.new()
424:	st.handle_binary_image_mode = GLTFState.HANDLE_BINARY_IMAGE_MODE_EMBED_AS_UNCOMPRESSED
425:	if append_ship_glb(doc, path, st) != OK:
426:		push_warning("glTF not loaded: " + path)
427:		return false
428:	for m in st.get_materials():
429:		if m is BaseMaterial3D:
430:			_compress_material(m as BaseMaterial3D)
431:	var scene := doc.generate_scene(st)
432:	scene.name = name
433:	_own(scene, scene)
434:	var ps := PackedScene.new()
435:	ps.pack(scene)
436:	var ok := ResourceSaver.save(ps, out, ResourceSaver.FLAG_COMPRESS) == OK
437:	scene.free()
438:	return ok

32:function verdictLine(output) {
33:  const lines = String(output || '').split(/\r?\n/).map(l => l.trim()).filter(Boolean);
34:  for (let i = lines.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) if (/^(PASS|FAIL)\b/.test(lines[i])) return lines[i];
35:  return '';
36:}

38:function parseFindings(output) {
39:  const passIds = [], failIds = [];
40:  let summary = null;
41:  for (const raw of String(output || '').split(/\r?\n/)) {
42:    const line = raw.trim();
43:    let m = /^PASS\s+(\S+)(?:\s|$)/.exec(line);
44:    if (m) { passIds.push(m[1]); continue; }
45:    m = /^FAIL\s+(\S+)(?:\s|$)/.exec(line);
46:    if (m) { failIds.push(m[1]); continue; }
47:    m = /^(\d+)\s+tests,\s+(\d+)\s+pass,\s+(\d+)\s+fail/.exec(line);
48:    if (m) summary = { total: +m[1], pass: +m[2], fail: +m[3] };
49:  }
50:  return { passIds, failIds, summary };
51:}
52:
53:function classifyFindings(run, baseline) {
54:  const { passIds, failIds, summary } = parseFindings(run.output);
55:  if (!summary) return { result: 'FAIL', detail: 'FAIL: missing findings summary' };
56:  if (passIds.length !== summary.pass || failIds.length !== summary.fail) {
57:    return { result: 'FAIL', detail: 'FAIL: parsed ' + passIds.length + ' pass / ' + failIds.length + ' fail lines, summary says ' + summary.pass + ' / ' + summary.fail };
58:  }
59:  const listed = new Set(baseline.knownFindingsFailures || []);
60:  const known = failIds.filter(id => listed.has(id));
61:  const unexpected = failIds.filter(id => !listed.has(id));
62:  const listedPasses = passIds.filter(id => listed.has(id));
63:  const seen = new Set([...passIds, ...failIds]);
64:  const listedMissing = [...listed].filter(id => !seen.has(id));
65:  if (listedPasses.length) return { result: 'FAIL', detail: 'FAIL: listed id(s) now pass, take them off the list: ' + listedPasses.join(', ') };
66:  if (unexpected.length) return { result: 'FAIL', detail: 'FAIL: ' + unexpected.length + ' new failure(s): ' + unexpected.join(', ') };
67:  if (listedMissing.length) return { result: 'FAIL', detail: 'FAIL: listed id(s) no longer run: ' + listedMissing.join(', ') };
68:  if (known.length) return { result: 'KNOWN', detail: 'KNOWN: ' + known.length + ' listed failure(s): ' + known.join(', ') };
69:  return { result: 'PASS', detail: 'PASS: all ' + summary.total + ' gated findings tests pass' };
70:}

72:function classifyPack(run, baseline) {
73:  const out = String(run.output || '');
74:  const m = /SUMMARY:\s*(\d+)\s+FAIL,\s*(\d+)\s+CHECK/.exec(out);
75:  if (!m) return { result: 'FAIL', detail: 'FAIL: missing check pack summary' };
76:  const fails = +m[1], checks = +m[2];
77:  const failLines = (out.match(/^FAIL\b/gm) || []).length;
78:  const ceiling = Number.isFinite(baseline.checksCeiling) ? baseline.checksCeiling : 0;
79:  if (run.code !== 0 || fails > 0 || failLines > 0) {
80:    return { result: 'FAIL', detail: 'FAIL: ' + fails + ' FAIL, ' + checks + ' CHECK' + (run.code !== 0 ? ' (exit ' + run.code + ')' : '') };
81:  }
82:  if (checks > ceiling) {
83:    return { result: 'FAIL', detail: 'FAIL: ' + checks + ' CHECK is above the baseline ceiling of ' + ceiling };
84:  }
85:  return { result: 'PASS', detail: 'PASS: within the pack baseline' };
86:}

88:function classifyDrift(run, baseline) {
89:  const out = String(run.output || '');
90:  let m = /DRIFT SUMMARY:[^\n]*?(\d+)\s+differed/.exec(out);
91:  if (!m) m = /constants:\s*\d+\s+entries compared,\s*\d+\s+matched,\s*(\d+)\s+differed/.exec(out);
92:  if (!m) return { result: 'FAIL', detail: 'FAIL: missing drift summary' };
93:  const differed = +m[1];
94:  const ceiling = Number.isFinite(baseline.driftDifferedCeiling) ? baseline.driftDifferedCeiling : 0;
95:  if (differed > ceiling) return { result: 'FAIL', detail: 'FAIL: ' + differed + ' differed is above the baseline ceiling of ' + ceiling };
96:  if (differed > 0) return { result: 'KNOWN', detail: 'KNOWN: ' + differed + ' constant difference(s) within the baseline' };
97:  return { result: 'PASS', detail: 'PASS: no constant drift' };
98:}

100:function classifyNaming(run, baseline) {
101:  const m = /naming_lint_game: (\d+) hard, (\d+) word/.exec(String(run.output || ''));
102:  if (!m) return { result: 'FAIL', detail: 'FAIL: missing naming summary' };
103:  const hard = +m[1], word = +m[2];
104:  const ceiling = Number.isFinite(baseline.namingHardHits) ? baseline.namingHardHits : 0;
105:  if (![0, 1].includes(run.code) || hard > ceiling) {
106:    return { result: 'FAIL', detail: 'FAIL: ' + hard + ' hard hits above the baseline of ' + ceiling + ', ' + word + ' word hits' };
107:  }
108:  return { result: 'PASS', detail: 'PASS: naming lint within the baseline' };
109:}

111:function classifyGeneric(run) {
112:  const out = String(run.output || '');
113:  const failLine = out.split(/\r?\n/).map(l => l.trim()).find(l => /^FAIL\b/.test(l)) || '';
114:  const v = verdictLine(out);
115:  if (run.code !== 0 || failLine) {
116:    return { result: 'FAIL', detail: failLine || (v && /^FAIL\b/.test(v) ? v : 'FAIL: exit ' + run.code) };
117:  }
118:  return { result: 'PASS', detail: v && /^PASS\b/.test(v) ? v : 'PASS: exit 0' };
119:}

def run(label, *args, allowed=(0,)):
    run = subprocess.run(args, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, errors=\"replace\", timeout=45)
    (root / (label + \".log\")).write_text(run.stdout + run.stderr, encoding=\"utf-8\")
    if run.returncode not in allowed or \"SCRIPT ERROR:\" in run.stdout + run.stderr:
        raise RuntimeError(f\"{label} exited {run.returncode}: {run.stdout}{run.stderr}\")
    return run

def hash_(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()

def link(source, dest):
    dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    assert source.samefile(dest) and source.stat().st_nlink == 2

+# Refs #1187: Ship file hardlink audit
+
+**Keep copying the ship files.** Stage 7 replaces the ship folder and its asset manifest, but its headless cache refresh rewrites `godot/gen/manifest.json` in place. On Windows, that refresh changed the SHA-256 of the source-side file in a scratch hardlink pair. Standalone cache rebuilds, copy jobs, and Godot reimport with safe save off have additional in-place writers.
+
+Reviewed `37361292a4421267f213dcb4553ec1532be229bc`. The inventory covers the checked-in writers to a project's `godot/assets/ships/` and `godot/gen/`, including launchers that install or seed those trees indirectly, and the test fixtures that exercise them. The current copier takes all of `gen/`, and skips `manifest.json`, `README.md`, `a4_props.gd`, `*.uid`, `test/`, and `previews/` under `assets/ships/`. It can copy existing `*.import` sidecars. [Copy and exclusions](../../../tools/pc/get_ship_files.bat#L28-L32), [checkout manifest verification](../../../tools/pc/get_ship_files.bat#L34-L59), [capture runner call](../../../tools/pc/work_issue.bat#L288-L289)
+

+## Copies into checkouts and review projects
+
+**Robocopy with overwrite allowed writes in place.** `/E` includes subdirectories and does not make the copy a replacement by rename. `/XF` and `/XD` only limit the paths selected. `/XC /XN /XO` together skip existing files under these commands, so those jobs add missing files without updating an existing link. The overlay moves three named GLBs aside before copying the new ship, but its maps and sidecars can still be overwritten in place. [Microsoft Robocopy options and missing-only example](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/robocopy#examples)

+## Windows verification
+
+Used same-volume hardlinks between files created in `%TEMP%`. Before and after each operation, checked the source file's SHA-256 and whether the checkout path still named the same file. The Stage 7 probe called `manifest_merge.install()` with a small checked-in GLB fixture and the real `build_assets.gd --ships-only` refresh on Godot 4.7.2. It isolated the publish/cache steps by supplying the fixture snapshot and a no-op readback. The builder reported one loaded ship. The separate `manifest_merge_selftest.py` passed its export-set, install, and rollback cases.
+
+| Scratch path or operation | Source SHA-256 before and after, first 12 digits | Checkout name after |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Stage 7 `gen/manifest.json` | `cb7ec0915763` to `cdbe5149468e` | Same file |
+| Stage 7 `assets/ships/manifest.json` | `cb7ec0915763` both times | Replaced |
+| Stage 7 ship GLB | `0d6090554083` both times | Replaced |
+| Stage 7 ship `.scn` | `37cda9ca8621` both times | Replaced |
+| Standalone `--ships-only --force`, existing damage `.scn` | `af4c5707042d` to `5fa27038a4e7` | Same file |
+| Robocopy `/E`, `copy /y`, and Xcopy `/y`, tested separately | `cba06b5736fa` to `06b263127d65` for each | Same file |
+| Robocopy `/E /XC /XN /XO` | `cba06b5736fa` both times | Same file, skipped |
+| PowerShell `Copy-Item` and Python `shutil.copy2` | `cba06b5736fa` to `59f19f34399b` for each | Same file |
+| Setting `LastWriteTimeUtc` through the link | `cba06b5736fa` both times | Same file, source timestamp changed |
+| `git checkout --` for a changed tracked file | `cba06b5736fa` both times | Replaced |
+| Godot `--import`, linked source JPG | `a7cf979c6438` both times, safe save on and off | Same file |
+| Godot `--import`, linked JPG `.import`, safe save on | `0858d24cf4b0` both times | Replaced |
+| Godot `--import`, linked JPG `.import`, safe save off | `0858d24cf4b0` to `5d2e90f53695` | Same file |
+
+The import test used a portable editor in scratch, a fresh `.godot` cache, and a preexisting `.import` with a marker comment. Godot removed the marker on reimport and generated the local `.ctex` in each case. The conditional live-build hash proof and hardlink rollout were skipped because the scratch probe proved the cache refresh would write through a link.
+
+## What would clear the blockers
+
+1. Stage the cache manifest, marker, field data, and each binary scene/resource in a private file on the checkout's volume, then replace the final name. Apply this to standalone generation and the T2 writers as well as Stage 7. Keep manifest paths pointing at their final files and keep the installer rollback and readback checks.
+2. Convert overwrite-capable copy routes to copy into fresh files and replace the destination names, including the fallback copy and the legacy/overlay installers. Replace or privatize a linked GLB before changing its timestamp. Keep the working copies free to update when the shared build also changes.
+3. Give each checkout its own editor sidecars and keep any writable glTF extraction outputs private, or make that import path use replacement independent of the user's editor setting. Keep the cache-writing tools away from the test junctions. Then check a real Stage 7 install and editor import in a linked checkout, comparing the shared build's file list, hashes and relevant timestamps before and after.

    if anchor:
        numbers = [int(n) for n in re.findall(r\"L(\\d+)\", anchor)]
        assert 0 < min(numbers) <= max(numbers) <= len(target.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8-sig\").splitlines()), link

+# Refs #1187: Ship file hardlink audit
+
+**Keep copying the ship files.** Stage 7 replaces the ship folder and its asset manifest, but its headless cache refresh rewrites `godot/gen/manifest.json` in place. On Windows, that refresh changed the SHA-256 of the source-side file in a scratch hardlink pair. Standalone cache rebuilds, copy jobs, and Godot reimport with safe save off have additional in-place writers.
+
+Reviewed `37361292a4421267f213dcb4553ec1532be229bc`. The inventory covers the checked-in writers to a project's `godot/assets/ships/` and `godot/gen/`, including launchers that install or seed those trees indirectly, and the test fixtures that exercise them. The current copier takes all of `gen/`, and skips `manifest.json`, `README.md`, `a4_props.gd`, `*.uid`, `test/`, and `previews/` under `assets/ships/`. It can copy existing `*.import` sidecars. [Copy and exclusions](../../../tools/pc/get_ship_files.bat#L28-L32), [checkout manifest verification](../../../tools/pc/get_ship_files.bat#L34-L59), [capture runner call](../../../tools/pc/work_issue.bat#L288-L289)

+## Copies into checkouts and review projects
+
+**Robocopy with overwrite allowed writes in place.** `/E` includes subdirectories and does not make the copy a replacement by rename. `/XF` and `/XD` only limit the paths selected. `/XC /XN /XO` together skip existing files under these commands, so those jobs add missing files without updating an existing link. The overlay moves three named GLBs aside before copying the new ship, but its maps and sidecars can still be overwritten in place. [Microsoft Robocopy options and missing-only example](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/robocopy#examples)

+## Windows verification
+
+Used same-volume hardlinks between files created in `%TEMP%`. Before and after each operation, checked the source file's SHA-256 and whether the checkout path still named the same file. The Stage 7 probe called `manifest_merge.install()` with a small checked-in GLB fixture and the real `build_assets.gd --ships-only` refresh on Godot 4.7.2. It isolated the publish/cache steps by supplying the fixture snapshot and a no-op readback. The builder reported one loaded ship. The separate `manifest_merge_selftest.py` passed its export-set, install, and rollback cases.

+
+The import test used a portable editor in scratch, a fresh `.godot` cache, and a preexisting `.import` with a marker comment. Godot removed the marker on reimport and generated the local `.ctex` in each case. The conditional live-build hash proof and hardlink rollout were skipped because the scratch probe proved the cache refresh would write through a link.
+
+## What would clear the blockers
+
+1. Stage the cache manifest, marker, field data, and each binary scene/resource in a private file on the checkout's volume, then replace the final name. Apply this to standalone generation and the T2 writers as well as Stage 7. Keep manifest paths pointing at their final files and keep the installer rollback and readback checks.
+2. Convert overwrite-capable copy routes to copy into fresh files and replace the destination names, including the fallback copy and the legacy and overlay installers. Replace or privatize a linked GLB before changing its timestamp. Apply the same rule to writes from the shared-build side, since an in-place write there reaches every linked checkout.
+3. Give each checkout its own editor sidecars and keep any writable glTF extraction outputs private, or make that import path use replacement independent of the user's editor setting. Keep the cache-writing tools away from the test junctions. Then check a real Stage 7 install and editor import in a linked checkout, comparing the shared build's file list, hashes and relevant timestamps before and after.

+# Ship file hardlink audit
+
+**Keep copying the ship files.** Stage 7 replaces the ship folder and its asset manifest, but its headless cache refresh rewrites `godot/gen/manifest.json` in place. On Windows, that refresh changed the SHA-256 of the source-side file in a scratch hardlink pair. Standalone cache rebuilds, copy jobs, and Godot reimport with safe save off have additional in-place writers.
+
+Refs #1187. Reviewed `37361292a4421267f213dcb4553ec1532be229bc`. The inventory covers the checked-in writers to a project's `godot/assets/ships/` and `godot/gen/`, including launchers that install or seed those trees indirectly, and the test fixtures that exercise them. The current copier takes all of `gen/`, and skips `manifest.json`, `README.md`, `a4_props.gd`, `*.uid`, `test/`, and `previews/` under `assets/ships/`. It can copy existing `*.import` sidecars. [Copy and exclusions](../../../tools/pc/get_ship_files.bat#L28-L32), [checkout manifest verification](../../../tools/pc/get_ship_files.bat#L34-L59), [capture runner call](../../../tools/pc/work_issue.bat#L288-L289)
+
+## Stage 7, Godot, and the asset tools
+
+| Writer and destination | What happens to an existing file | Code |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `7_export.bat` and `export7.py`, recipe output | **In place in the recipe output.** GLB, maps and JSON go under `%JOB%\export\%CODE%`. With `INSTALL_TO` set, the batch sends the export to the installer below. | [Batch export and install](../../../tools/recipe/7_export.bat#L17-L45), [recipe job path](../../../tools/recipe/env.bat#L12-L16), [Blender writes](../../../tools/recipe/export7.py#L483-L529) |
+| `manifest_merge.py --install`, `assets/ships/<CODE>/` and `assets/ships/manifest.json` | **Replaces.** Checks a snapshot, then copies into a fresh incoming folder. Moves the old ship folder aside, publishes the incoming folder, and swaps a staged manifest over the live one with `os.replace`. The `shutil.copy2` and `write_text` calls here target staging or backup paths. | [Snapshot](../../../tools/recipe/manifest_merge.py#L86-L100), [staging](../../../tools/recipe/manifest_merge.py#L122-L151), [publish and rollback](../../../tools/recipe/manifest_merge.py#L160-L199) |
+| `manifest_merge.py --install`, `gen/ships/<CODE>.scn` | **Replaces.** Moves the old scene to `previous/ship.scn` before running the builder, so the builder creates the new scene at a vacant path. Only the incoming ship is presented to the builder. The staged export omits the old damage/wreck GLBs, so this route drops the old references from the manifest and leaves the old damage/wreck `.scn` files alone. | [Managed inputs](../../../tools/recipe/manifest_merge.py#L120-L144), [scene move and refresh](../../../tools/recipe/manifest_merge.py#L167-L178), [optional scene writes](../../../godot/render/build_assets.gd#L360-L366) |
+| `manifest_merge.py --install`, `gen/manifest.json` | **In place.** Copies the old cache manifest to a backup, then leaves the live name in place for `build_assets.gd --ships-only` to open with `FileAccess.WRITE`. If install fails, rollback replaces the checkout's name from the backup. The original file shared with the build has already been written. | [Backup](../../../tools/recipe/manifest_merge.py#L145-L146), [refresh and rollback](../../../tools/recipe/manifest_merge.py#L167-L193), [headless arguments](../../../tools/recipe/manifest_merge.py#L226-L235), [manifest write](../../../godot/render/build_assets.gd#L100-L113) |
+| `manifest_merge.py ENTRY PROJECT CODE`, `assets/ships/manifest.json` | **Replaces.** The look-bench overlay's manifest-only command writes a new file in `manifest.bak_*` and publishes it with `os.replace`. | [Staged write and swap](../../../tools/recipe/manifest_merge.py#L65-L82), [overlay call](../../../tools/pc/jobs/lb_overlay_ship.bat#L41) |
+| `build_assets.gd`, both modes, `gen/manifest.json` | **In place.** `_save_manifest()` opens the live file during builds and at the end of `--ships-only`. Full generation also opens the live manifest directly at the end. | [Ships-only call](../../../godot/render/build_assets.gd#L50-L63), [full-build write](../../../godot/render/build_assets.gd#L90-L92), [progress and manifest write](../../../godot/render/build_assets.gd#L100-L113) |
+| `build_assets.gd`, full mode, `gen/asteroids.json` and `gen/v3.txt` | **In place.** Opens the final paths with `FileAccess.WRITE` when copying field placements and marking a completed build. | [Field and version marker](../../../godot/render/build_assets.gd#L75-L89) |
+| `build_assets.gd`, cache resources | **In place on rebuild.** Compressed `ResourceSaver.save` writes straight to `gen/ships`, `damage`, `wreck`, `hulls`, `hi`, `rocks`, and `sky.res`. A current entry can skip the write. A stale or forced rebuild can overwrite the original file if it is still linked. Runtime headless script runs use the direct-write path. | [Ship, damage, wreck paths](../../../godot/render/build_assets.gd#L330-L366), [scene save](../../../godot/render/build_assets.gd#L421-L438), [hull](../../../godot/render/build_assets.gd#L244-L274), [high-detail](../../../godot/render/build_assets.gd#L286-L319), [rocks](../../../godot/render/build_assets.gd#L491-L528), [sky](../../../godot/render/build_assets.gd#L531-L543), [Godot binary saver](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/core/io/resource_format_binary.cpp#L1976-L1988), [compressed file open](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/core/io/file_access_compressed.cpp#L75-L84) |
+| Godot editor `--import`, GLBs and external maps | Reads the GLB and existing external JPG/PNG bytes. Imported scenes/textures and checksums go into `.godot/imported/`. A scene configured to extract embedded textures can also write generated images beside the GLB, using the same safe-save setting as sidecars. The headless ship-cache builder reads external maps directly and embeds them in its in-memory glTF state. | [Godot import path](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/core/io/resource_importer.cpp#L504-L507), [Godot glTF extraction writes](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/modules/gltf/gltf_document.cpp#L2080-L2141), [cache builder map reads](../../../godot/render/build_assets.gd#L421-L470) |
+| Godot editor `--import`, `*.import` and `*.uid` | **Replaces with editor safe save on, writes in place if off.** The importer opens `<asset>.import` for writing beside the source, even when generated assets go to `.godot/imported/`. The scan can also create or regenerate script UID sidecars. Safe save is on by default and the Windows backend uses a temporary sibling and `ReplaceFileW` when enabled. | [Single and grouped sidecar writes](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/editor/file_system/editor_file_system.cpp#L2499-L2508), [single asset](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/editor/file_system/editor_file_system.cpp#L2736-L2745), [UID sidecars](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/editor/file_system/editor_file_system.cpp#L1286-L1303), [editor setting](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/editor/settings/editor_settings.cpp#L611-L615), [setting applied](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/editor/editor_node.cpp#L7763-L7768), [Windows open and replace](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.7.2-stable/drivers/windows/file_access_windows.cpp#L184-L244) |

The A4 manifest generator writes `manifest.json` and previews directly if its destination is set to the project tree. +## Copies into checkouts and review projects
+
+**Robocopy with overwrite allowed writes in place.** `/E` includes subdirectories. `/XF` and `/XD` limit the paths selected. `/XC /XN /XO` together skip existing files under these commands, so those jobs add missing files without updating an existing link. The overlay moves the old damage and wreck GLBs aside, then can overwrite the main GLB, maps, and sidecars in place. [Overlay copy](../../../tools/pc/jobs/lb_overlay_ship.bat#L31-L40), [Microsoft Robocopy options and missing-only example](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/robocopy#examples)

+## Tests that touch the trees

These wrappers use the cache as input and never run a rebuild or editor import through the junction. +## Windows verification
+
+Used same-volume hardlinks between files created in `%TEMP%`. Before and after each operation, checked the source file's SHA-256 and whether the checkout path still named the same file. The Stage 7 probe called `manifest_merge.install()` with a small checked-in GLB fixture and the real `build_assets.gd --ships-only` refresh on Godot 4.7.2. It isolated the publish/cache steps by supplying the fixture snapshot and a no-op readback. The builder reported one loaded ship. The separate `manifest_merge_selftest.py` passed its export-set, install, and rollback cases.
+
+| Scratch path or operation | Source SHA-256 before and after, first 12 digits | Checkout name after |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Stage 7 `gen/manifest.json` | `cb7ec0915763` to `cdbe5149468e` | Same file |
+| Stage 7 `assets/ships/manifest.json` | `cb7ec0915763` both times | Replaced |
+| Stage 7 ship GLB | `0d6090554083` both times | Replaced |
+| Stage 7 ship `.scn` | `37cda9ca8621` both times | Replaced |
+| Standalone `--ships-only --force`, existing damage `.scn` | `af4c5707042d` to `5fa27038a4e7` | Same file |
+| Robocopy `/E`, `copy /y`, and Xcopy `/y`, tested separately | `cba06b5736fa` to `06b263127d65` for each | Same file |
+| Robocopy `/E /XC /XN /XO` | `cba06b5736fa` both times | Same file, skipped |
+| PowerShell `Copy-Item` and Python `shutil.copy2` | `cba06b5736fa` to `59f19f34399b` for each | Same file |
+| Setting `LastWriteTimeUtc` through the link | `cba06b5736fa` both times | Same file, source timestamp changed |
+| `git checkout --` for a changed tracked file | `cba06b5736fa` both times | Replaced |
+| Godot `--import`, linked source JPG | `a7cf979c6438` both times, safe save on and off | Same file |
+| Godot `--import`, linked JPG `.import`, safe save on | `0858d24cf4b0` both times | Replaced |
+| Godot `--import`, linked JPG `.import`, safe save off | `0858d24cf4b0` to `5d2e90f53695` | Same file |
+
+The import test used a portable editor in scratch, a fresh `.godot` cache, and a preexisting `.import` with a marker comment. Godot removed the marker on reimport and generated the local `.ctex` in each case. The conditional live-build hash proof and hardlink rollout were skipped because the scratch probe proved the cache refresh would write through a link.
+
+## What would clear the blockers
+
+1. Stage the cache manifest, marker, field data, and each binary scene/resource in a private file on the checkout's volume, then replace the final name. Apply this to standalone generation and the T2 writers as well as Stage 7. Keep manifest paths pointing at their final files and keep the installer rollback and readback checks.
+2. Convert overwrite-capable copy routes to copy into fresh files and replace the destination names, including the fallback copy and the legacy and overlay installers. Replace or privatize a linked GLB before changing its timestamp. Apply the same rule to writes from the shared-build side, since an in-place write there reaches every linked checkout.
+3. Give each checkout its own editor sidecars and keep any writable glTF extraction outputs private, or make that import path use replacement independent of the user's editor setting. Keep the cache-writing tools away from the test junctions. Then check a real Stage 7 install and editor import in a linked checkout, comparing the shared build's file list, hashes and relevant timestamps before and after.

+# Ship file hardlink audit
+
+**Keep copying the ship files.** Stage 7 replaces the ship folder and its asset manifest, but its headless cache refresh rewrites `godot/gen/manifest.json` in place. On Windows, that refresh changed the SHA-256 of the source-side file in a scratch hardlink pair. Standalone cache rebuilds, copy jobs, and Godot reimport with safe save off have additional in-place writers.
+
+Refs #1187. Reviewed `37361292a4421267f213dcb4553ec1532be229bc`. The inventory covers the checked-in writers to a project's `godot/assets/ships/` and `godot/gen/`, including launchers that install or seed those trees indirectly, and the test fixtures that exercise them. The current copier takes all of `gen/`, and skips `manifest.json`, `README.md`, `a4_props.gd`, `*.uid`, `test/`, and `previews/` under `assets/ships/`. It can copy existing `*.import` sidecars. [Copy and exclusions](../../../tools/pc/get_ship_files.bat#L28-L32), [checkout manifest verification](../../../tools/pc/get_ship_files.bat#L34-L59), [capture runner call](../../../tools/pc/work_issue.bat#L288-L289)

+## Copies into checkouts and review projects
+
+**Robocopy with overwrite allowed writes in place.** `/E` includes subdirectories. `/XF` and `/XD` limit the paths selected. `/XC /XN /XO` together skip existing files under these commands, so those jobs add missing files without updating an existing link. The overlay moves the old damage and wreck GLBs aside, then can overwrite the main GLB, maps, and sidecars in place. [Overlay copy](../../../tools/pc/jobs/lb_overlay_ship.bat#L31-L40), [Microsoft Robocopy options and missing-only example](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/robocopy#examples)
+

+## Windows verification
+
+Used same-volume hardlinks between files created in `%TEMP%`. Before and after each operation, checked the source file's SHA-256 and whether the checkout path still named the same file. The Stage 7 probe called `manifest_merge.install()` with a small checked-in GLB fixture and the real `build_assets.gd --ships-only` refresh on Godot 4.7.2. It isolated the publish/cache steps by supplying the fixture snapshot and a no-op readback. The builder reported one loaded ship. The separate `manifest_merge_selftest.py` passed its export-set, install, and rollback cases.
+
+| Scratch path or operation | Source SHA-256 before and after, first 12 digits | Checkout name after |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Stage 7 `gen/manifest.json` | `cb7ec0915763` to `cdbe5149468e` | Same file |
+| Stage 7 `assets/ships/manifest.json` | `cb7ec0915763` both times | Replaced |
+| Stage 7 ship GLB | `0d6090554083` both times | Replaced |
+| Stage 7 ship `.scn` | `37cda9ca8621` both times | Replaced |
+| Standalone `--ships-only --force`, existing damage `.scn` | `af4c5707042d` to `5fa27038a4e7` | Same file |
+| Robocopy `/E`, `copy /y`, and Xcopy `/y`, tested separately | `cba06b5736fa` to `06b263127d65` for each | Same file |
+| Robocopy `/E /XC /XN /XO` | `cba06b5736fa` both times | Same file, skipped |
+| PowerShell `Copy-Item` and Python `shutil.copy2` | `cba06b5736fa` to `59f19f34399b` for each | Same file |
+| Setting `LastWriteTimeUtc` through the link | `cba06b5736fa` both times | Same file, source timestamp changed |
+| `git checkout --` for a changed tracked file | `cba06b5736fa` both times | Replaced |
+| Godot `--import`, linked source JPG | `a7cf979c6438` both times, safe save on and off | Same file |
+| Godot `--import`, linked JPG `.import`, safe save on | `0858d24cf4b0` both times | Replaced |
+| Godot `--import`, linked JPG `.import`, safe save off | `0858d24cf4b0` to `5d2e90f53695` | Same file |
+
+The import test used a portable editor in scratch, a fresh `.godot` cache, and a preexisting `.import` with a marker comment. Godot removed the marker on reimport and generated the local `.ctex` in each case. The conditional live-build hash proof and hardlink rollout were skipped because the scratch probe proved the cache refresh would write through a link.
+
+## What would clear the blockers
+
+1. Stage the cache manifest, marker, field data, and each binary scene/resource in a private file on the checkout's volume, then replace the final name. Apply this to standalone generation and the T2 writers as well as Stage 7. Keep manifest paths pointing at their final files and keep the installer rollback and readback checks.
+2. Convert overwrite-capable copy routes to copy into fresh files and replace the destination names, including the fallback copy and the legacy and overlay installers. Replace or privatize a linked GLB before changing its timestamp. Apply the same rule to writes from the shared-build side, since an in-place write there reaches every linked checkout.
+3. Give each checkout its own editor sidecars and keep any writable glTF extraction outputs private, or make that import path use replacement independent of the user's editor setting. Keep the cache-writing tools away from the test junctions. Then check a real Stage 7 install and editor import in a linked checkout, comparing the shared build's file list, hashes and relevant timestamps before and after.
